messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English about two adult friends making a small decision together. Let their different preferences and personalities show through naturally. The decision should matter only a little. Keep the scene grounded, specific, and lightly humorous without generic summaries or a dramatic ending.

“Window seat.”

“No.”

Sam stopped beside the diner booth. “Why not?”

“Because you always get the window seat.”

“You’re the one who wanted to sit down.”

“And you’re the one who got here first.”

Sam pointed at the two empty seats. “This one has better lighting.”

Riley looked toward the window. “We’re eating pancakes, not taking headshots.”

“You don’t understand.”

“I understand that you’re being dramatic before coffee.”

Sam put a hand over his chest. “I thought you knew me better.”

“I do. That’s why I’m sitting here.”

He stared at her for a second, then laughed. “Fine.”

They slid into the booth.

Riley picked up the menu. “Chocolate chip?”

“Blueberry.”

“You’re boring.”

“You’re predictable.”

“Exactly.”

The server came by, and they both ordered without looking up.

Sam glanced at Riley’s plate when the food arrived.

“Don’t even think about it.”

“I wasn’t.”

“You were.”

He smiled. “Maybe a little.”

Riley pushed one blueberry-covered pancake toward him. “Take it.”

Sam looked genuinely surprised. “Really?”

“Yes.”

“Wow.”

“Don’t make me take it back.”

He picked it up immediately. “Best decision you’ve made all morning.”
